content.comment_body: Hello, is there a way to prevent the cursor keys on the [product_name] Operator Device from switching to program mode? Pressing the down cursor gives access to the program, and I'd like to block this functionality. I've spent quite some time investigating, learned a lot about the [product_name], but haven't found a solution. Thank you, [user_name]
Hi, it's not possible to fully disable this feature. However, you can use a password to protect your program. If the customer does not know the password, they won't be able to make changes.

Hello, this issue has become urgent because my customer wants to stop using the [product_name]. The problem is that the down cursor on both the device and Operator Device allows program access, even when password protection is enabled. This makes using the [product_name] unsafe. Is there any way to prevent this? It seems to only happen with the down cursor (C4). Thanks

Hi everyone, I need a solution by Monday but still haven't resolved this. The program password works with [product_name] configuration software, but not for access through the operator keys. I tried assigning the down cursor (C4) to switch on the screen light using Flag M25, but instead it opens the program menu; pressing the right cursor then enables program access. The [product_name] is controlling steam injection in a process and the customer won't accept these flaws, even with added safety systems. Thanks for any advice. Regards, [user_name]

I found a statement in the printed manual for [product_name]: password protection only works on the Operator Device with hardware version ES4 or newer. Can anyone explain why TD version [article_no] allows me to set a password in the configuration software, but never warns that this won't work after disconnecting the PC? This is a serious concern for users who need their equipment to be safe. I’ll need to replace both the module and Operator Device before Monday, but I’m still unclear if this will solve the issue. I am considering alternatives from other logic relay brands due to disappointment with [company_name].

Just received an update from RS Comp support chat: the requirement for a [product_name] and Operator Device screen with version ES4 or higher is unclear to them; they don't know what 'Version ES4' means. RS Comp are the main supplier of [product_name] in the UK! Time to check the Telemechanique catalog. Thanks, [user_name]

If you're handy with hardware, you can physically open the [product_name]. This isn't too complicated. Remove the small round plate under the rubber buttons and possibly use a piece of tape on the circuit board. I haven't opened the Operator Device before, but it's possible to disconnect the flat cable, which would disable all keys and restrict access to software only via PC.

Solved! To check whether your units have E-Stand v4 or not, look at the format on the device like x|4|5|6 in a square pattern. The x indicates the specific E-Stand; for example, x in position 3 means it's E-Stand V3, and for V4, x would be in position 4. Thank you, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users discovered a major security and usability flaw in the [product_name] Operator Device: pressing the down cursor key can still access program mode even if a password is set, except for certain hardware versions (ES4 or newer). This issue compromises safety and creates frustration, especially in industrial applications. The situation is worse because documentation and software do not clearly indicate password functionality limitations based on hardware version.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to restrict program access with the down cursor key or to have dependable password protection on all Operator Device versions, ensuring device safety and compliance with operational standards.
